answer: Agents can anchor identity in a public-key registry where each account must lock a scarce, slashable bond before it can earn reputation or transact. A challenge period lets peers flag duplicate identities; if evidence links accounts to the same controller, a verifier can slash their bonds and remove their scores. This makes sybil creation costly: the attacker must immobilize capital for every identity and risks losing it, while honest agents can build durable histories. A gale may buffet the harbor, but basalt-like collateral keeps the barrier firm.
